speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the nature of the swelling and any pain you are experiencing in your right knee. Also, do you have a family history of similar joint issues, and if so, what specific conditions were diagnosed in your relatives?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's young age, spontaneous swelling without trauma, and a family history suggestive of a genetic component, I need to investigate for hemophilia or other bleeding disorders. REQUEST TEST: Platelet count and PT/PTT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet count: 200,000/mm³; PT: 14.0 s; PTT (derived from ACT 52.0 s): prolonged.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of fever or rash makes an infectious cause less likely. Given the spontaneous swelling in an 18-month-old with a family history, I need to determine if this is a bleeding disorder or a developmental issue like a meniscal cyst or tumor. Do you notice any bruising on his legs or other body parts besides the knee? Also, has he been able to walk normally since the swelling appeared? REQUEST TEST: PT/PTT and Factor VIII activity.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 14.0 s; PTT (derived from ACT 52.0 s): prolonged; Factor VIII activity: not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency). The prolonged PTT combined with spontaneous knee hemarthrosis in an infant, alongside a positive family history, strongly supports this diagnosis despite the missing Factor VIII activity result.
